date: # Wilhelm Loehe's calendars of saints, one name or more for every day of the year, as translated by
# Benjamin T. G. Mayes (October 2001): variant 1859, "The Sanctoral Calendar of Wilhelm Loehe" (Haus-,
# Schul- und Kirchenbuch für Christen des lutherischen Bekenntnisses, Zweiter Theil, Stuttgart 1859,
# pp. 114-140; loehe_kirchenbuch.pdf); variant 1868, "The Sanctoral Calendar of Wilhelm Loehe's
# Martyrologium" (Martyrologium. Zur Erklärung der herkömmlichen Kalendernamen, Nürnberg 1868;
# loehe_martyrologium.pdf), which Loehe corrected and cut to about one name a day.
# full_name is the entry as Mayes gives it, its abbreviations spelled out (his key: Ab. = Abbot,
# Ap. = Apostle, B. = Bishop, C. = Confessor, D. = Deacon, M. = Martyr, P. = Presbyter, V. = Virgin,
# W. = Widow; doubled, plural); name, for the wheel, leaves out its dates and the Bible references
# to read about the saint.  1 January (the Circumcision), 6 January (the Epiphany) and 25 December
# (the Nativity) are days.csv's.  Feasts of the Lord and of Mary that the 1859 book heads with Latin
# names are principal (white), the apostles' and evangelists' days and St. Michael's festivals, in
# the Common Service Book's colors as for ELHB; Loehe gives no colors.
# 24 February: St. Matthias (in leap years 25 February, the 1859 book notes; kept on the 24th here).
# Links (as for the LCMS): CPH's post for the day where LSB keeps the saint, else a Wikipedia article
# (the Wikipedia calendars of saints, Lutheran, Anglican and the General Roman Calendar of 1954),
# else a Wikipedia search for the name and its place.
